newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen losing steam Mon.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen losing steam Mon.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the second consecutive session and turnover was up, but analysts said the market was likely to continue to lose steam after Thursday's 1.6-percent rise that followed Wednesday's 3.2-percent gain.

"The higher turnover is a good sign...but stocks might be mixed on Monday because the market is usually not too dynamic after a long weekend," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Markets are closed on Friday for All Saints Day.
Other analysts said the Thursday buying after price fixing -- in the face of slightly stronger selling -- was not strong enough to signal major growth on Monday.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.6 percent to 13,497.9 points and turnover rose 29.5 percent to 115.8 million zlotys ($41.2 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 47 to 18 with 15 stocks flat.
Analysts said biggest mover construction firm Espebepe surged 9.5 percent as speculators sought to take advantage of the firm's previous 45.2-percent drop on news it might go bankrupt.
Continuous trade turnover was at 2.8 million zlotys ($1 million) with biggest mover food trader and producer Animex down 6.7 percent.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 2.5 percent to 144 zlotys ($51.2) in the regular bourse session and were flat at the same price in 15.6-million-zloty ($5.6 million) continuous trade.
